Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

speech noun

the power or manner of speaking

also power of speech, the gift of speech, way of speaking

classical

Cic. Off. 1.50: ejus autem vinculum est ratiō et ōrātiō
Cic. Off. 1.12: ad ōrātiōnis et ad vītae societātem

ōrātiō, ōrātiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

speech, the power of speaking; a way of speaking

Lewis & Short: “speech, the power or faculty of speech, the habit or use of language”. With reason it is what sets people apart from animals, which are ratiōnis et ōrātiōnis expertēs (Off. 1.50). Also a person’s way of speaking.

Examples

  • ejus autem vinculum est ratiō et ōrātiō, quae docendō, discendō, commūnicandō, disceptandō, jūdicandō conciliat inter sē hominēs conjungitque nātūrālī quādam societāte

    and its bond is reason and speech, which by teaching, learning, sharing, debating and judging bring people together and join them in a kind of natural fellowshipCic. Off. 1.50

  • ex ejus linguā melle dulcior fluēbat ōrātiō

    speech sweeter than honey flowed from his tongueCic. Sen. 31

See also speech, language, talk, communication.
